text: The Marsh Serpent strikes at once, slamming its head down on Borro's shield, and Nib goes for its neck.
His knives skid off the jade scales in a shower of sparks.
Nib lands and stares at his notched blades. They don't bite.
Then it blasts scalding steam at Borro until his shield glows red.
Borro's burns blister Jaeha's palms. Yerin is already healing them.
Its coils slide toward the fish section, the tail dragging through spilled ice.
Frost spreads over the scales, and the tail jerks away as if burned.
Jaeha watches that tail, and his eyes narrow.
His palms are too burned to hold the notebook, so Yerin holds it while he writes. Cold-blooded. Cold makes it slow.
He phones Seoa. Who has the freezer keys? The kimchi granny's son. And that lane is a dead end.
Turn the lane into a freezer, walk the serpent in, and shut the door behind it.
Yerin protests: he can't even hold a pencil. He'll do what he always does. He's the bait.
He runs right past its head, waving his arms, behind Borro's red-hot shield. It takes the bait.
The kimchi granny and her son haul open every freezer, and Seoa kicks open a refrigerated truck.
Forty metres of freezers and mist, ending in a wall. Jaeha runs down it, and the serpent follows.
Where its hot scales meet the cold, the whole lane fills with fog.
Frost creeps over the jade and gold. The steam thins.
Jaeha runs out of lane, his back to the frozen wall. The jaws rise over him, slower now.
He gives them his polite trap-tester smile. Sorry, sir. He walks in first. It's his job.
Then Borro slams his shield across the lane's mouth like a door. The door is shut.
It thrashes, smashing doors and trucks, but every move is slower than the last.
Its frozen tail hammers Borro's shield, and Jaeha feels every blow. One hundred and thirty percent.
Its yellow eye goes cloudy. Only the violet crack on its brow still pulses.
Jaeha points a shaking hand. Nib has thirty seconds of field form left. The crack on its brow: the scales are brittle now.
Nib runs up the serpent's frozen coils like a staircase.
He drives both knives through the frosted scales, and they shatter like ice, right into the crack.
The serpent rears, smashes the lights, and bursts into a storm of violet ash and glittering frost.
Ash and frost settle like snow. Jaeha slides down the wall to sit.
A window: break boss defeated. The break is closing.
A second window gets a long, tired look. Harvest the core, thirty million won. No other option.
Three times now, only harvest. He doesn't like it. He presses it anyway.
Operator level five, a third summon slot, and Route Alignment, the meter for his next call, hits ninety percent.
The Association's hunters finally arrive and step away from Borro. The core goes to a relief fund, says Choi. Does the market get a new bridge?
The next morning, His Summons Go First is on every phone: three point one million views in a day.
Everyone watches the giant hold up the bridge. Some call it CGI. The rest chant Trap Rats.
The news calls them unusual husks: fourteen saved on a falling bridge.
At school, Seoa's classmates mob her desk. Is the trap-tester really her brother? Unfortunately, she says.
The kimchi granny tells a TV crew: the big husk held the bridge, and she held her alley.
Then Bomi's subscriber count ticks over. Ninety-nine thousand nine hundred and ninety-nine. One hundred thousand.
She screams at the sky outside her parents' restaurant, open for the first time in weeks.
The sponsors called. They get to keep the restaurant.
On the rooftop, Bomi sets up a thumbnail shoot, and Borro strikes a proud pose.
Nib is asked for one smile, for the thumbnail. No.
Bomi pushes his mouth into a smile with two fingers. His eyes stay dead.
Her title is ready: the Trap Rats. One of them wouldn't smile.
Yerin holds a cold can to Jaeha's burned palm. She didn't freeze once. He saw. She was the bravest one there.
That evening, a crowd outside the market chants it. Trap Rats. The insult is now a chant.
Thursday night. Kanghan Tower, sixty storeys of glass over Yeouido.
At last, the man in silver glasses shows his face. Director Baek Taegun, fifty-four, Kanghan Group Core Division.
A file: Gate 0912 survivor Kang Jaeha. Two unusual husks. Operator probability: ninety-one percent.
He watches the giant hold the bridge. Husks don't hold bridges. And they don't choose who to save.
One call: have Mok invite him on the B-grade raid for heroes, and watch his husks when he's in danger.
In its glass case, a boss core pulses slowly, like a heartbeat.
In Kanghan's guild hall, forty flawless husks hold the same lunge in perfect rows, conducted by a woman with a silver baton.
She turns from them, all in white, like the hall belongs to her. A husk holds out a tablet playing the clip.
On it, a masked shape moves faster than any husk. Her smile freezes. Husks don't move like that.
One flick of her baton, and all forty heads turn to look.
Friday night, Jaeha sneezes violently over his tteokbokki. Nib is not impressed.
Borro's welcome dinner at last: bubbling tteokbokki, the whole team, and Borro sitting on the roof to be level with them.
Seoa hands him one rice cake, saved from the break. Eat.
Borro chews very, very slowly. He likes rice cakes. Definitely.
Then Jaeha's phone buzzes. Mok Hangyu of Black Hound invites the hero of Mangwon Market to walk into a B-grade raid with them.
The laughter dies. Seoa says no. Yerin reminds him: Mok left him to die.
Nib's ears go flat. Doors. Mok likes closing them.
Bomi says what everyone in Seoul can see. It's a trap. Jaeha knows. He's a trap-tester.
On a clean page he writes: B-grade raid, Mok, a crossbow, a door that closes.
His eyes go cold and level.
The notebook snaps shut. That means the plan is ready.
Jaeha stands up. Tell Mok yes. This time, he's the one setting the trap.
